newsitem.title: RWANDA: Genocide condemned appeal against sentence.
newsitem.headline: Genocide condemned appeal against sentence.

text.p: The first two defendants sentenced to death in Rwanda for acts of genocide in 1994 have filed appeals within the statutory 15-day deadline.
"I have decided to appeal because I am innocent. I've always pleaded not guilty," former medical assistant Deogratias Bizimana told Reuters in his isolation cell in Kibungo prison on Wednesday.
He shares the cell with Egide Gatanaze, condemned to death with him on January 3 after trial.

Prison director Manasse Sebagabo said Gatanaze had also lodged an appeal. Under Rwanda's Genocide Law passed in 1996, those convicted must file an appeal within 15 days of conviction. It must be heard within three months by the Court of Appeal. If the sentences are upheld the two men will be executed by firing squad.

An estimated 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in three months in 1994 by the former hardline Hutu regime. Bizimana and Gatanaze are among scores of accused due to appear as Category One defendants, charged with playing leading roles in the genocide.
"I've applied for legal help through Avocats sans Frontieres (Lawyers Without Borders) but I do not know when it is coming through," Bizimana said.
The isolation cell shared by the two condemned men is separate from the rest of the prison.
"They have been in there for two days now," said Sebagabo.
On Wednesday Kibungo's prison population was swollen by a further 119 inmates transferred from a communal detention centre in nearby Zaza parish.

Food, firewood and medical care at the prison are provided by the International Committee of the Red Cross. The prisoners share communal dormitories which though crowded are not as packed as other prisons in Rwanda containing 90,000 genocide suspects.
Authorities said medical problems included dysentery, malaria and tuberculosis.
"My sentence is based upon complicity between witnesses and public officials," Bizimana said.
